title: Present Perfect vs Past Simple
objective: Talk about experiences and results now (present perfect) and finished past events (past simple). Use for / since correctly.

sections.heading: Form
sections.en: have / has + past participle (worked, been, done, seen, written).
sections.fr: have/has + participe passé. Attention : le present perfect ne correspond PAS toujours au passé composé.
examples: I have visited Ghana three times.
She has just finished her report.
Have you ever spoken in public?
We haven't received the results yet.

sections.heading: When to use it
sections.en: 1) Life experience with no time given (ever / never). 2) A past action with a result now (just, already, yet). 3) A situation that started in the past and continues now (for / since).
sections.fr: Pas de date précise → present perfect. Dès qu'il y a un moment terminé (yesterday, in 2020, last week, ago) → past simple.

sections.heading: Present perfect or past simple?
sections.en: Finished time = past simple. Unfinished time or no time = present perfect.
table: I have lived in Lomé for 5 years. (I still live there)
I lived in Kara for 5 years. (I don't now)
Have you ever been to Canada?
When did you go to Canada?
I've lost my keys. (I can't open the door)

sections.heading: for / since
sections.en: for + a period (for two years, for a long time). since + a starting point (since 2021, since January, since I was a child).
sections.fr: « depuis » se traduit par for (durée) ou since (point de départ), avec le present perfect — pas le présent simple !
examples: I have studied English for six months. (not: I study English since six months)
He has worked here since 2022.

vocab.definition: at any time in your life (questions)
vocab.example: Have you ever worked abroad?

vocab.definition: until now (questions and negatives, at the end)
vocab.example: I haven't finished yet.
I've already sent the email.

vocab.definition: something good you succeeded in doing
vocab.example: Winning the data challenge was a great achievement.

practice.explanation: Situation that started in the past and continues → present perfect + for.

quiz.prompt: ___ you ever ___ a presentation in English?
quiz.explanation: Life experience with "ever" → present perfect: have + past participle (given).

quiz.prompt: I ___ my degree in 2023.
quiz.explanation: "In 2023" = finished time → past simple.

quiz.prompt: We have known each other ___ ten years.
quiz.explanation: Ten years = a period → for.

quiz.prompt: Has the client answered ___?
quiz.explanation: "Yet" at the end of questions and negatives.

quiz.prompt: "I live in Lomé since 2019" is correct.
quiz.explanation: Since/for with an ongoing situation → present perfect: I have lived in Lomé since 2019.

quiz.prompt: Oh no! I ___ my password. I can't log in.
quiz.explanation: Past action with a present result → present perfect.

quiz.prompt: She ___ (be) to London twice.
quiz.explanation: Experience → has been (been = gone and come back).

quiz.prompt: When ___ you start learning English?
quiz.explanation: Questions with "when" ask for a finished time → past simple.

rememberErrors.why: Present perfect with since/for for an ongoing situation.

title: Education and studying abroad
objective: Talk about your studies, applications and academic life — useful for IELTS Speaking Part 1 and interviews.

sections.heading: Collocations
sections.en: English uses fixed word partners. Learn them together.
sections.fr: Attention aux faux amis : « passer un examen » = take an exam ; « réussir » = pass.

sections.heading: Talking about plans
sections.en: I'm planning to do a master's in data science. I've applied to three universities. I'm waiting for an offer.

vocab.example: I'm taking the IELTS in June.
She passed with a band 7.

vocab.definition: money paid to study at a university
vocab.example: Tuition fees are lower in some European countries.

vocab.definition: detailed study to discover new facts
vocab.example: He does research on machine learning.
I enrolled in an online course.

vocab.definition: to finish university with a degree
vocab.example: I graduated in 2021.
The language requirement is IELTS 6.5.

practice.prompt: I'm going to ___ the TOEFL next month.

quiz.prompt: She ___ her exam! She got 8.0.
quiz.explanation: Success → passed.

quiz.prompt: I've applied ___ a scholarship.
quiz.explanation: Apply for a scholarship / job / visa; apply to a university.

quiz.prompt: The minimum ___ is a bachelor's degree.
quiz.explanation: Requirement = condition needed.

quiz.prompt: "I did many researches" is correct.
quiz.explanation: Research is uncountable: I did a lot of research.

quiz.prompt: You must pay the ___ before the semester starts.
quiz.explanation: Tuition fees = money paid for studies.

quiz.prompt: He ___ from university last year. (finished with a degree)
quiz.explanation: Graduate = obtain your degree.

rememberErrors.wrong: I will pass the IELTS on Monday (= sit it)
rememberErrors.right: I will take the IELTS on Monday.

title: Modal verbs: obligation, advice, possibility
objective: Give advice, express obligation and possibility with must, have to, should, might, can, could.

sections.heading: Form
sections.en: Modal + base verb, no "to", no -s: she should study (not: she shoulds / she should to study).

sections.heading: Obligation
sections.en: "Must" = obligation from the speaker or rules. "Have to" = external obligation. "Don't have to" = it's not necessary. "Mustn't" = it's forbidden.
sections.fr: Piège : « don't have to » = pas obligé ; « mustn't » = interdit.
examples: You must wear a badge in the building.
I have to submit the visa form by Friday.
You don't have to come — it's optional.
You mustn't share your password.

sections.heading: Advice
sections.en: should / ought to / you'd better.
examples: You should practise speaking every day.
You'd better leave now or you'll miss the bus.

sections.heading: Possibility & deduction
sections.en: might / may / could = possible; must = almost certain; can't = impossible.
examples: It might rain later.
He must be tired — he worked all night.
That can't be true.

vocab.example: Attendance is mandatory.

vocab.definition: you can choose to do it or not
vocab.example: The second module is optional.
I recommend that you read every day.

practice.prompt: You ___ smoke in the hospital. It's forbidden.

quiz.prompt: Tomorrow is a holiday, so I ___ go to work.
quiz.explanation: Not necessary → don't have to.

quiz.prompt: If you want to improve, you ___ listen to podcasts.
quiz.explanation: Advice → should + base verb.

quiz.prompt: She isn't answering. She ___ be in a meeting.
quiz.explanation: Possibility → might.

quiz.prompt: "He musts finish today" is correct.
quiz.explanation: Modals never take -s: He must finish today.

quiz.prompt: You've worked 14 hours. You ___ be exhausted!
quiz.explanation: Logical deduction (almost certain) → must.

quiz.prompt: Students ___ to show their ID card at the exam. (external obligation, use "have")
quiz.explanation: External rule → have to.

rememberErrors.why: No "to" after modal verbs (except have to / ought to).

rememberErrors.wrong: You mustn't come (= it's not necessary)

title: Meetings: giving and defending your opinion
objective: Give an opinion, agree, disagree politely and interrupt in a meeting.

sections.heading: Giving an opinion
sections.en: Start with an opinion phrase, give a reason, then an example.
examples: In my opinion, we should launch the beta first, because we need real feedback. For example, …
I think it would be better to…
From my point of view, …

sections.heading: Agreeing and disagreeing politely
sections.en: In professional English, soften disagreement.
sections.fr: En anglais professionnel, on adoucit le désaccord : « I see your point, but… » plutôt que « No, you are wrong ».
examples: I completely agree with you.
That's a good point.
I see what you mean, but I'm not sure that's the best option.
I'm afraid I disagree.

sections.heading: Interrupting and clarifying
sections.en: Sorry to interrupt, but… / Could you clarify what you mean by…? / Just to make sure I understand, …

vocab.example: From my point of view, the price is too high.

vocab.definition: to have the same opinion as someone
vocab.example: I agree with Sarah.
Could you clarify the deadline?
I suggest that we start with the mobile version.

practice.prompt: Which is the most polite disagreement?
options: I see your point, but I think the deadline is too short.
practice.explanation: Acknowledge the other view, then add "but" + your reason.

quiz.prompt: "I am agree with you" is correct.
quiz.explanation: "Agree" is a verb: I agree with you.

quiz.prompt: I suggest ___ the meeting to Friday.
quiz.explanation: Suggest + -ing (or suggest that we move). Never "suggest to do".

quiz.prompt: Sorry to ___, but I have a quick question.
quiz.explanation: Sorry to + base verb: Sorry to interrupt.

quiz.prompt: Order the words.
quiz.answer: could you clarify what you mean
quiz.explanation: Indirect question inside: "what you mean" (no inversion).

rememberErrors.right: I suggest that you call / I suggest calling.
rememberErrors.why: Suggest is never followed by object + to.

title: Conditional sentences (zero, first, second)
objective: Talk about general truths, real future possibilities and imaginary situations.

sections.heading: Zero conditional — always true
sections.en: If + present, present.
examples: If you heat ice, it melts.
If I drink coffee late, I can't sleep.

sections.heading: First conditional — real possibility
sections.en: If + present simple, will + base verb. Never "will" in the if-clause.
sections.fr: Pas de « will » après « if » (comme en français : « s'il pleut », pas « s'il pleuvra »).
examples: If I get the scholarship, I will move to Canada.
If it rains, we'll stay inside.
You'll fail unless you study. (unless = if not)

sections.heading: Second conditional — imaginary or unlikely
sections.en: If + past simple, would + base verb. Use "were" for all persons in careful English.
sections.fr: If + prétérit, would + verbe : équivalent de « si + imparfait, conditionnel ».
examples: If I had more time, I would learn Chinese.
If I were you, I would take the IELTS first.
What would you do if you lost your job?

vocab.example: I won't go unless you come with me.
You can use my laptop as long as you are careful.
Take an umbrella in case it rains.

practice.prompt: If it ___ tomorrow, we will cancel the trip.
practice.explanation: First conditional: if + present simple (no will).

quiz.prompt: If I ___ rich, I would travel around the world.
quiz.explanation: Second conditional: if + past simple (were is preferred).

quiz.prompt: If you study every day, you ___ (pass) the exam.
quiz.explanation: First conditional result: will + base verb.

quiz.prompt: If I were you, I ___ accept the offer.
quiz.explanation: Advice with "If I were you" → would.

quiz.prompt: "If I will have time, I will call you" is correct.
quiz.explanation: No will in the if-clause: If I have time, I will call you.

quiz.prompt: You can't enter ___ you have a ticket.
quiz.explanation: Unless = if not.

quiz.prompt: If you mix blue and yellow, you ___ green.
quiz.explanation: General truth → zero conditional: if + present, present.

rememberErrors.wrong: If I will finish early, I will call.
rememberErrors.right: If I finish early, I will call.

rememberErrors.wrong: If I would have money, I would buy it.
rememberErrors.right: If I had money, I would buy it.
rememberErrors.why: Past simple after if in the 2nd conditional.

title: Technology and the digital world
objective: Describe technology, apps and their impact — a frequent IELTS / TOEFL topic.

sections.heading: Useful structures
sections.en: Technology allows people to… / makes it easier to… / has led to… / One drawback is that…
sections.fr: « permettre de » = allow someone to / enable someone to (jamais « permit to »).
examples: Mobile money allows people to pay without a bank account.
Smartphones have made it easier to learn languages.
One drawback is that people spend too much time online.

vocab.definition: a machine or tool, e.g. a phone or tablet
vocab.example: The app works on any device.

vocab.definition: that you can trust to work well
vocab.example: We need a reliable Internet connection.
The main drawback is the price.

vocab.definition: a newer version; to make something more modern
vocab.fr: mise à jour / mettre à jour
vocab.example: Install the latest update.
The data is stored on your phone.
The app enables learners to study offline.
AI has made major breakthroughs.

practice.prompt: This app ___ students to practise offline.
practice.explanation: Allow + object + to + verb. (Let + object + base verb, without to.)

quiz.prompt: The main ___ of social media is addiction.
quiz.explanation: Drawback = disadvantage.

quiz.prompt: My connection isn't ___ — it cuts every hour.
quiz.explanation: Reliable = works consistently.

quiz.prompt: Technology has made it easier ___ abroad.
quiz.explanation: make it easier + to + verb.

quiz.prompt: "Smartphones let people to work anywhere" is correct.
quiz.explanation: Let + object + base verb: let people work.

quiz.prompt: Please install the latest ___ to fix the bug.
quiz.explanation: Update = newer version.

rememberErrors.right: It allows us to save time / It saves time.

title: The passive voice
objective: Describe processes, news and facts when the action is more important than who does it — essential for IELTS Writing Task 1.

sections.heading: Form
sections.en: be (in the right tense) + past participle.
table: They have built a new road.
A new road has been built.

sections.heading: When to use it
sections.en: When the doer is unknown, obvious or unimportant, and in formal/scientific writing. Add "by + agent" only if it is useful.
sections.fr: Le passif est très fréquent en anglais (souvent traduit par « on » en français : « on m'a dit » → « I was told »).
examples: English is spoken in many countries.
The data was collected in 2025.
I was told that the office is closed.

sections.heading: Describing a process
sections.en: First, the cocoa beans are harvested. Then they are dried in the sun. After that, they are transported to the port.

vocab.example: Coffee is harvested by hand.

vocab.definition: to produce in large quantities in a factory
vocab.example: The parts are manufactured in Asia.
Afterwards, the product is packed.

quiz.prompt: The bridge ___ in 2019.
quiz.explanation: Past simple passive (finished time): was + built.

quiz.prompt: The results ___ next week.
quiz.explanation: Future passive: will be + past participle.

quiz.prompt: A new hospital ___ (build) in our town. It opened last month. (present perfect passive)
quiz.explanation: Present perfect passive: has been + built.

quiz.prompt: "I was told that the meeting is cancelled" is a correct passive sentence.
quiz.explanation: Correct — passive with "tell" (= on m'a dit).

quiz.prompt: The form must ___ before Friday.
quiz.explanation: Modal passive: must be + past participle.

quiz.prompt: Order the words.
quiz.answer: the beans are dried in the sun
quiz.explanation: Process description in the present simple passive.

title: Environment and society
objective: Discuss environmental problems and solutions with precise vocabulary.

sections.heading: Problem → cause → solution
sections.en: A strong answer names the problem, explains a cause and proposes a solution.
examples: Deforestation is a serious problem. It is mainly caused by farming and charcoal production. One solution would be to promote gas for cooking.

vocab.definition: damage to air, water or land by harmful substances
vocab.example: Air pollution is rising in big cities.
Deforestation affects rainfall.

vocab.definition: energy from sources that do not run out (sun, wind)
vocab.example: Solar panels produce renewable energy.
Plastic waste blocks the drains.
We must reduce our energy consumption.

vocab.definition: long-term change in the Earth's temperature and weather
vocab.example: Climate change affects farmers.

practice.prompt: Solar and wind are sources of ___ energy.

quiz.prompt: We should ___ the use of plastic bags.
quiz.explanation: Reduce = make less.

quiz.prompt: "There are many pollutions in the city" is correct.
quiz.explanation: Pollution is uncountable: There is a lot of pollution.

quiz.prompt: Cutting down forests is called ___.
quiz.explanation: Deforestation.

quiz.prompt: Don't ___ water: turn off the tap.
quiz.explanation: Waste = use badly or unnecessarily.

quiz.prompt: Floods are partly ___ by blocked drains.
quiz.explanation: Passive: are caused by.
